edges.name: Persian Gulf Crude Oil via the Strait of Hormuz
edges.estimated_global_share: In the most recent pre-disruption baseline (1H2025), about 20.9 million barrels per day of oil transited the Strait of Hormuz -- roughly 20% of global petroleum consumption and about a quarter of total global maritime-traded oil -- plus over 20% of global LNG trade, per the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Since a disruption beginning February 28, 2026, actual flows have run well below that baseline: EIA reports no laden LNG tankers transited the strait between March 1 and April 24, 2026 (cutting off over 20% of global LNG supply), and China alone cut waterborne crude imports by 3.9 million barrels per day quarter-on-quarter in 2Q26, including a 910,000 b/d drop in cargoes sourced from Iraq. EIA had not published an updated aggregate oil-transit-volume figure for the strait itself as of its most recent relevant analysis (July 31, 2026).

edges.name: Oncology Generic Sterile Injectable Chemotherapy Drug Shortages
commodities: generic sterile injectable chemotherapy drugs (e.g. cisplatin, carboplatin, methotrexate, leucovorin, dacarbazine, fludarabine phosphate, azacitidine)
other low-margin generic oncology supportive-care injectables

vulnerability_factors.text: Persistent thin profit margins on generic sterile injectable oncology drugs discourage manufacturers from maintaining backup capacity or staying in the market - a 2025 peer-reviewed analysis in Cancer Journal found essential injectable cancer drugs in shortage cost an average of about $2 per vial, versus roughly $1,423 for comparable non-shortage cancer drugs

Extreme few-manufacturer concentration for individual drugs - the same 2025 Cancer Journal study found all identified U.S. manufacturers of cisplatin (6 of 6) and of azacitidine (9 of 9) were reporting shortages simultaneously, and that more than 80% of the oncology drugs it studied had experienced at least one manufacturer exit the market before the shortage began

Manufacturing-quality failures at concentrated overseas plants, most notably an FDA inspection of Intas Pharmaceuticals' India facility supplying Accord Pharma (roughly a third of the U.S. injectable methotrexate market before 2022), which found quality-control records that were "discarded, missing, and purposefully destroyed," according to a 2025 multinational survey published in The Oncologist

Hospital pharmaceutical purchasing is itself concentrated - the 2025 Cancer Journal analysis found Group Purchasing Organizations control an estimated 90% of U.S. hospital pharmaceutical procurement through just four major organizations, reinforcing low-price, single-supplier contracting that leaves little room for redundant capacity
Complex, hazardous, and capital-intensive sterile cytotoxic manufacturing processes that limit the number of facilities able or willing to produce these drugs at all

edges.estimated_global_share: A 2025 peer-reviewed Cancer Journal analysis found all identified U.S. manufacturers of cisplatin (6 of 6) and azacitidine (9 of 9) were reporting shortages simultaneously, and that more than 80% of the oncology drugs it studied had at least one manufacturer exit the market before the shortage began; separately, Accord Pharma - supplied by a single Intas Pharmaceuticals plant in India - held roughly one-third of the U.S. injectable methotrexate market before a 2022 quality-driven shutdown, per a 2025 multinational survey published in The Oncologist.
